components.note: 疒 (illness) — 疒 is the sickness radical, as in 病, 痛, 症; 癌 is cancer.
嵒 (yán) — near sound — 癌 is ái.
疒 (illness) — 疒 is the sickness radical, as in 病, 痛, 痕; 症 is an illness or its symptoms.
正 (zhèng) — same sound — 症 is zhèng, like 正; 正 also sounds out 证 zhèng.

example.hanzi: 早期发现癌症可以提高治愈的机会。
example.pinyin: Zǎoqī fāxiàn áizhèng kěyǐ tígāo zhìyù de jīhuì.
example.english: Discovering cancer early can improve the chances of a cure.
example.fact: 癌 is pronounced ái in Mandarin rather than the "regular" phonetic reading yán (matching its component 嵒) — several sources attribute this deliberate divergence to hospitals wanting to avoid dangerous mix-ups between 癌症 ("cancer") and the similarly-pronounced 炎症 ("inflammation") when spoken aloud.

examples.hanzi: 他的爷爷因为癌症去世了。
examples.pinyin: Tā de yéye yīnwèi áizhèng qùshì le.
examples.english: His grandfather passed away from cancer.

examples.hanzi: 医生说她的癌症已经好了。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng shuō tā de áizhèng yǐjīng hǎo le.
examples.english: The doctor said her cancer is gone.

components.note: 爵 (wine cup) — 爵 was an ancient three-legged bronze wine cup, a mark of rank — so a noble title, as in 公爵.
士 (scholar, soldier) — usually read as an axe or weapon, so a warrior or gentleman (士兵, 博士). Memory aid: 士 has the longer bar on top, 土 (earth) on the bottom.

example.hanzi: 他被英国女王封为爵士。
example.pinyin: Tā bèi Yīngguó nǚwáng fēng wéi juéshì.
example.english: He was knighted by the Queen of England.
example.fact: 爵士 does double duty as two unrelated words sharing the same two characters: the older sense "knight, Sir" (a hand 寸 holding the ceremonial wine goblet 爵, the ancient symbol of noble rank) and the newer sense "jazz," a straightforward phonetic loan from English with no connection to the original meaning.

examples.hanzi: 每个星期五晚上,这家酒吧都有爵士演出。
examples.pinyin: Měi ge xīngqīwǔ wǎnshang, zhè jiā jiǔbā dōu yǒu juéshì yǎnchū.
examples.english: Every Friday night, this bar has a jazz performance.

examples.hanzi: 我喜欢在咖啡馆里听爵士。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan zài kāfēiguǎn lǐ tīng juéshì.
examples.english: I like listening to jazz in cafés.

components.note: 衣 (clothes; 衤 on the left) — the outer garment.
毛 (fur) — a fur coat worn outside: the outside, the surface, then to show.
日 (sun) — the sun beside the moon: two light sources, so bright and clear.
月 (moon) — as in 朋, 期, 有; here it brightens the night.

example.hanzi: 研究结果表明,运动对健康很有帮助。
example.pinyin: Yánjiū jiéguǒ biǎomíng, yùndòng duì jiànkāng hěn yǒu bāngzhù.
example.english: The research results indicate that exercise is very helpful for health.
example.fact: 表明 is a workhorse of formal and academic writing — introducing evidence, data, or a conclusion ("研究表明...", "the research indicates...") — and sounds noticeably stiff in casual conversation, where speakers reach for the plainer 说明 or just 说 instead.

examples.hanzi: 这个数字表明经济正在变好。
examples.pinyin: Zhège shùzì biǎomíng jīngjì zhèngzài biàn hǎo.
examples.english: This number shows the economy is getting better.

examples.hanzi: 他表明了自己不同意的态度。
examples.pinyin: Tā biǎomíng le zìjǐ bù tóngyì de tàidu.
examples.english: He made clear that he doesn't agree.

components.note: 扌 (hand, 提手旁) — marks hand actions, as in 打 hit, 推 push, 拉 pull; 抬 is lifting or carrying.
台 (tái) — same sound: 抬 tái. 台 also sounds out 胎 tāi and 苔 tái.

example.hanzi: 请帮我抬一下这张桌子。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ tái yíxià zhè zhāng zhuōzi.
example.english: Please help me lift this table.
example.fact: 抬 is used for lifting something up, and for two or more people carrying a heavy thing between them. 抬头 means to raise one's head. In colloquial speech 抬杠 describes arguing just for the sake of arguing.

examples.hanzi: 他抬头看了看天空。
examples.pinyin: Tā tái tóu kàn le kan tiānkōng.
examples.english: He looked up at the sky.

examples.hanzi: 我们两个人把沙发抬上楼。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen liǎng ge rén bǎ shāfā tái shàng lóu.
examples.english: The two of us carried the sofa upstairs.

components.note: 飞 (fly) — simplified from 飛, a bird with spread wings.
彳 (step) — left half of a crossroads: 行 pictures a crossroads, so to go, and (háng) a row or trade.

example.hanzi: 这架飞机的飞行时间大约十个小时。
example.pinyin: Zhè jià fēijī de fēixíng shíjiān dàyuē shí gè xiǎoshí.
example.english: This plane's flight time is about ten hours.
example.fact: 飞行 is reserved for controlled, mechanical flight — airplanes, pilots, aviation — while a bird or insect's more ordinary fluttering about is just 飞 alone; the added 行 ("to travel, to move along") frames 飞行 specifically as sustained, directional travel through the air.

examples.hanzi: 明天的飞行时间大约是两个小时。
examples.pinyin: Míngtiān de fēixíng shíjiān dàyuē shì liǎng ge xiǎoshí.
examples.english: Tomorrow's flight time is about two hours.

examples.hanzi: 鸟儿在天空中自由飞行。
examples.pinyin: Niǎor zài tiānkōng zhōng zìyóu fēixíng.
examples.english: Birds fly freely in the sky.

components.note: 耂 (old) — 老 pictures an old person with long hair leaning on a staff; the short form 耂 is also in 考 test and 孝 filial.
公 (public) — 八 over 厶: dividing 八 what is private 厶; so "shared, public, fair".

example.hanzi: 我老公每天都做饭。
example.pinyin: Wǒ lǎogōng měitiān dōu zuò fàn.
example.english: My husband cooks every day.
example.fact: 老公 is casual, spoken-register Mandarin — the neutral, written-register word for "husband" is 丈夫 — so using 老公 in a formal document would feel about as out of place as calling your own spouse "hubby" in a business letter.

examples.hanzi: 我老公今天晚上要加班。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ lǎogōng jīntiān wǎnshang yào jiābān.
examples.english: My husband has to work overtime tonight.

examples.hanzi: 你老公真体贴,每天都来接你。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ lǎogōng zhēn tǐtiē, měi tiān dōu lái jiē nǐ.
examples.english: Your husband is so thoughtful and picks you up every day.

components.note: 刂 (knife; 刀) — marks cutting, as in 别 separate, 刻 carve, 划 slice; 剑 is a sword, a blade.
佥 (qiān) — loose sound hint (jiàn); same part in 检 jiǎn, 险 xiǎn and 验 yàn.

example.hanzi: 他从小就喜欢练剑。
example.pinyin: Tā cóng xiǎo jiù xǐhuan liàn jiàn.
example.english: He has loved practicing swordsmanship since childhood.
example.fact: 剑 is the straight, double-edged sword, unlike the single-edged 刀 (dāo). The pair appears in the idiom 刀光剑影, 'flash of blades and shadow of swords', for tense fighting, and 剑 gives 剑桥 (Cambridge).

examples.hanzi: 他在电影里用一把长剑。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài diànyǐng li yòng yì bǎ cháng jiàn.
examples.english: In the movie he uses a long sword.

examples.hanzi: 我弟弟买了一把玩具剑。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ dìdi mǎi le yì bǎ wánjù jiàn.
examples.english: My younger brother bought a toy sword.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — marks cloth and hangings, as in 布 cloth, 帽 hat; 幅 is the width of cloth and a measure word for pictures.
畐 (fú) — same sound: 幅 fú. 畐 also sounds out 福 fú and 副 fù.

example.hanzi: 墙上挂着一幅画。
example.pinyin: Qiáng shàng guà zhe yì fú huà.
example.english: A painting hangs on the wall.
example.fact: 幅 is the measure word for paintings, photos, maps and posters: 一幅画, 一幅地图. 张 also works for flat things, but 幅 feels more artistic. It also builds 幅度 (range, extent) and 篇幅 (length of a text).

examples.hanzi: 这幅画是哪位画家画的?
examples.pinyin: Zhè fú huà shì nǎ wèi huàjiā huà de?
examples.english: Which artist painted this picture?

examples.hanzi: 他送了我一幅书法。
examples.pinyin: Tā sòng le wǒ yì fú shūfǎ.
examples.english: He gave me a piece of calligraphy.

components.note: 大 (big person) — a person with a line above the head, marking the sky above; tiān = heaven, sky, day.
才 (talent, just) — a sprout pushing out of the ground. 才 also sounds out 材 cái and 财 cái.

example.hanzi: 莫扎特是音乐天才。
example.pinyin: Mòzhātè shì yīnyuè tiāncái.
example.english: Mozart was a musical genius.
example.fact: 天才 literally means "heaven-born talent" (天 "heaven" + 才, a character depicting a sprout just breaking through the soil) — framing genius as an innate gift from birth, in contrast to 人才 ("talented person," 人 "human"), which describes ability built through training and effort.

examples.hanzi: 大家都说他是一个数学天才。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu shuō tā shì yí ge shùxué tiāncái.
examples.english: Everyone says he's a math genius.

examples.hanzi: 这个孩子很有画画的天才。
examples.pinyin: Zhège háizi hěn yǒu huà huà de tiāncái.
examples.english: This kid has a real talent for drawing.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and pouring, as in 河, 海, 清: 注 is to pour in.
主 (zhǔ) is a close sound clue for zhù; 主 also in 住 zhù, 柱 zhù and 驻 zhù.

example.hanzi: 请注意安全。
example.pinyin: Qǐng zhùyì ānquán.
example.english: Please pay attention to safety.
example.fact: 注 is the core of 注意 (pay attention), 注射 (to inject), 注册 (to register), 关注 (to follow closely, or follow someone online) and 注释 (annotation). The idea of 'pouring' attention in explains the modern uses.

examples.hanzi: 开车时要注意看路。
examples.pinyin: Kāichē shí yào zhùyì kàn lù.
examples.english: Pay attention to the road when you drive.

examples.hanzi: 请先注册一个账号。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng xiān zhùcè yí ge zhànghào.
examples.english: Please register an account first.

components.note: 工 (work) — a carpenter's tool shape: work, craftsman. 工 is a sound series: 红 hóng, 江 jiāng, 功 gōng, 空 kōng.
具 (tool) — two hands 廾 (the bottom 八) hold something valuable above — to provide, and a tool, as in 工具; 具 also sounds out 惧 jù.

example.hanzi: 锤子是一种常见的工具。
example.pinyin: Chuízi shì yì zhǒng chángjiàn de gōngjù.
example.english: A hammer is a common tool.
example.fact: 工具 reaches well past physical hammers and wrenches to cover any "instrument" or "means" for getting something done — 学习工具 ("learning tools"), 工具书 ("reference book," literally "tool book") — extending 工 ("work, labor") into anything that helps get work done.

examples.hanzi: 手机已经成了我们生活中的重要工具。
examples.pinyin: Shǒujī yǐjīng chéng le wǒmen shēnghuó zhōng de zhòngyào gōngjù.
examples.english: Phones have become an important tool in our lives.

examples.hanzi: 我爸爸的工具箱里什么工具都有。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bàba de gōngjùxiāng lǐ shénme gōngjù dōu yǒu.
examples.english: My dad's toolbox has every kind of tool.

components.note: 骨 (bone) — 骨 is the bone radical, as in 骼, 髓, 体; 骨 is bones, with ⺼ (flesh) beneath.
页 (head, page) — in traditional 頭 (豆 + 页): 页 is an old picture of a head, as in 顶, 领, 额. 头 dropped both parts.
大 (big) — the bottom. Memory aid: a big 大 body with two dots ⺀ like eyes above — the head, as in 头发. The dictionary's reading is loose.

example.hanzi: 小狗正在啃一根骨头。
example.pinyin: Xiǎo gǒu zhèngzài kěn yì gēn gǔtou.
example.english: The puppy is gnawing on a bone.
example.fact: Beyond its literal anatomical sense, 骨头 extends metaphorically to a person's inner character — 硬骨头 ("hard bone") describes someone tough and unyielding, echoing how English also reaches for "spine" and "backbone" as stand-ins for moral fortitude.

examples.hanzi: 鱼骨头太多,小心别卡住。
examples.pinyin: Yú gǔtou tài duō, xiǎoxīn bié kǎ zhù.
examples.english: There are too many fish bones, be careful not to choke.

examples.hanzi: 他摔了一跤,伤到了骨头。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuāi le yì jiāo, shāng dào le gǔtou.
examples.english: He fell and injured a bone.

components.note: 辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 迷; 送 is walking someone off, or delivering.
纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 线, 组; 给 is to supply thread, then to give.
合 (hé) is only a loose sound clue; same part in 答 dá, 拾 shí, 恰 qià.

example.hanzi: 我把这本书送给你。
example.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ zhè běn shū sònggěi nǐ.
example.english: I'm giving you this book as a present.
example.fact: 送给 pairs two overlapping "giving" verbs back to back — 送 ("to give a gift, to see someone off") and 给 ("to give, for") — a common Mandarin strategy for pinning down exactly which sense of an ambiguous single-syllable verb is meant, here ruling out 送's other sense of "to escort, see off."

examples.hanzi: 他想把这个礼物送给妈妈。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng bǎ zhège lǐwù sòng gěi māma.
examples.english: He wants to give this gift to his mom.

examples.hanzi: 朋友送给我一盆花。
examples.pinyin: Péngyou sòng gěi wǒ yì pén huā.
examples.english: My friend gave me a pot of flowers.

components.note: 言 (speech) — 言 is the traditional full form of the 讠 radical for speech and language: 说, 话, 语, 请.

example.hanzi: 我想学一门新语言。
example.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng xué yì mén xīn yǔyán.
example.english: I want to learn a new language.
example.fact: 言 is a classical word for speech and survives in compounds: 语言 (language), 发言 (to speak up), 留言 (leave a message), 方言 (dialect). It is the source of the 讠 radical used in many speaking characters.

examples.hanzi: 我们一言为定!
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yì yán wéi dìng!
examples.english: It's a deal!

examples.hanzi: 他一言不发地离开了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yì yán bù fā de líkāi le.
examples.english: He left without saying a word.

components.note: 足 (foot) — marks feet and walking, as in 跑 run, 跳 jump, 路 road; 踩 is stepping on something.
采 (cǎi) — same sound: 踩 cǎi. 采 also sounds out 彩 cǎi and 菜 cài.

example.hanzi: 对不起,我踩到你的脚了。
example.pinyin: Duìbuqǐ, wǒ cǎi dào nǐ de jiǎo le.
example.english: Sorry, I stepped on your foot.
example.fact: 踩 means to put your foot down on something. It has a lively slang life: 踩雷 ('step on a mine') means to pick something disappointing, such as a bad restaurant, and 踩坑 is similar.

examples.hanzi: 小心,别踩到水坑。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn, bié cǎi dào shuǐkēng.
examples.english: Careful, don't step in the puddle.

examples.hanzi: 他踩着自行车去上班。
examples.pinyin: Tā cǎi zhe zìxíngchē qù shàngbān.
examples.english: He pedals his bike to work.

components.note: 心 (heart) — 心 is the heart, as in 想, 思, 念; 忍 is a blade 刃 over the heart — enduring pain.
刃 (rèn) — near sound — 忍 is rěn; 刃 is a blade with an edge marked by a dot.

example.hanzi: 我忍不住笑了。
example.pinyin: Wǒ rěnbuzhù xiào le.
example.english: I couldn't help laughing.
example.fact: 忍不住 means 'can't help doing' something. 忍 also builds 忍耐 (endure) and 残忍 (cruel). A line from the Analects, 小不忍则乱大谋, says a lack of patience in small things ruins big plans.

examples.hanzi: 疼得我忍不住叫了出来。
examples.pinyin: Téng de wǒ rěn bu zhù jiào le chūlái.
examples.english: It hurt so much that I couldn't help crying out.

examples.hanzi: 我实在忍受不了这个噪音。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shízài rěnshòu bu liǎo zhège zàoyīn.
examples.english: I really can't stand this noise.

components.note: 酉 (wine jar) — fermented drinks: 酒, 醉 drunk, 酸 sour; 醒 is sobering up, then waking.
星 (xīng) sounds exactly like 醒 (tone differs).
来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.

example.hanzi: 他半夜醒来,再也睡不着了。
example.pinyin: Tā bànyè xǐnglái, zài yě shuì bu zháo le.
example.english: He woke up in the middle of the night and couldn't fall back asleep.
example.fact: 醒 (酉 "wine jar" + phonetic 星) originally described sobering up after drinking — 醒来, adding the directional complement 来 ("to come," marking a change occurring toward the present), extends that same "clearing of the mind" from intoxication to ordinary sleep.

examples.hanzi: 今天早上我六点就醒来了。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān zǎoshang wǒ liù diǎn jiù xǐnglái le.
examples.english: I woke up at six this morning.

examples.hanzi: 她醒来的时候,发现已经是中午了。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐnglái de shíhou, fāxiàn yǐjīng shì zhōngwǔ le.
examples.english: When she woke up, she found it was already noon.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — cloth family: 布, 带, 帽. Memory aid: a market stall with a cloth banner 巾 under a roof 亠, i.e. a 市 market.
柿 (shì, persimmon) — contains 市 as a sound part, same sound shì.
长 (long, grow) — simplified from 長, an old person with long hair. Read cháng "long" or zhǎng "to grow, elder".

example.hanzi: 新市长上任后推出了不少新政策。
example.pinyin: Xīn shìzhǎng shàngrèn hòu tuīchū le bù shǎo xīn zhèngcè.
example.english: After taking office, the new mayor introduced quite a few new policies.
example.fact: 市长 literally means "city chief" — 市 ("city") plus 长, here read zhǎng ("head, chief") rather than its other reading cháng ("long") — the same zhǎng "head of" pattern recurs across titles like 校长 ("school principal") and 队长 ("team captain").

examples.hanzi: 市长今天要去学校参观。
examples.pinyin: Shìzhǎng jīntiān yào qù xuéxiào cānguān.
examples.english: The mayor is visiting a school today.

examples.hanzi: 市长在电视上向市民问好。
examples.pinyin: Shìzhǎng zài diànshì shang xiàng shìmín wènhǎo.
examples.english: The mayor greeted citizens on TV.

components.note: 田 (field) — a field above 力 (strength): a man is one who works the fields with strength.
土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.

example.hanzi: 班里的男生比女生多。
example.pinyin: Bān lǐ de nánshēng bǐ nǚshēng duō.
example.english: There are more boys than girls in the class.
example.fact: 男生 and its counterpart 女生 began as school vocabulary (生, "student," as in 学生) for "male/female student," but everyday spoken Mandarin has broadened both well past the classroom to mean simply "guy" and "girl" for young people in general.

examples.hanzi: 我们班的男生都喜欢踢足球。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bān de nánshēng dōu xǐhuan tī zúqiú.
examples.english: The boys in our class all like playing soccer.

examples.hanzi: 那个男生是新来的转学生。
examples.pinyin: Nàge nánshēng shì xīn lái de zhuǎnxuéshēng.
examples.english: That boy is a new transfer student.

components.note: 发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).
身 (body, bow) — 身 is a worn-down picture of a bow, with a hand 寸 drawing it — 射 is to shoot.

example.hanzi: 科学家们成功发射了一颗卫星。
example.pinyin: Kēxuéjiāmen chénggōng fāshè le yì kē wèixīng.
example.english: The scientists successfully launched a satellite.
example.fact: 射's own components picture a drawn bow (身) plus a hand releasing the arrow (寸) — a vivid literal image of shooting that 发射 broadens from arrows to rockets, bullets, and even photons or radio waves ("to emit").

examples.hanzi: 火箭明天早上八点发射。
examples.pinyin: Huǒjiàn míngtiān zǎoshang bā diǎn fāshè.
examples.english: The rocket will launch at eight tomorrow morning.

examples.hanzi: 这种装置可以发射信号。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng zhuāngzhì kěyǐ fāshè xìnhào.
examples.english: This kind of device can transmit signals.

components.note: 之 (of, go) — oldest form is a foot leaving a starting line: "to go". Now it is a literary particle meaning "of" or "it".
内 (inside) — a person or something entering 入 inside an enclosure 冂: inside, as in 内容.

example.hanzi: 这些问题必须在三天之内解决。
example.pinyin: Zhèxiē wèntí bìxū zài sāntiān zhīnèi jiějué.
example.english: These problems must be solved within three days.
example.fact: 之 is a classical, literary linking particle that functioned much like 的 — most of its old grammatical roles have faded from everyday speech, but it survives fossilized inside a handful of fixed formal compounds, including 之内, 之后 ("after"), and 之前 ("before").

examples.hanzi: 请在一个小时之内回复我。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài yí ge xiǎoshí zhīnèi huífù wǒ.
examples.english: Please reply to me within an hour.

examples.hanzi: 房间之内很安静，什么声音都没有。
examples.pinyin: Fángjiān zhīnèi hěn ānjìng, shénme shēngyīn dōu méiyǒu.
examples.english: It was very quiet inside the room, with no sound at all.

components.note: 耂 (old) — shown in 老 old and 者; 考 first meant an aged person (the same word as 老), then to examine.
丂 (kǎo) gives the sound; also in 巧 qiǎo, 烤 kǎo and 拷 kǎo.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and language: 说 say, 请 ask, 读 read; testing often involves questions.
式 (shì) sounds exactly like 试 — a reliable sound clue.

example.hanzi: 下星期我们有一场重要的考试。
example.pinyin: Xià xīngqī wǒmen yǒu yì chǎng zhòngyào de kǎoshì.
example.english: Next week we have an important exam.
example.fact: 考 alone already means "to test, to examine" and by extension "to ponder" (as in 思考), while 试 alone means "to try." 考试 layers one on top of the other — almost "to try at being tested" — a compositional logic that stays fairly transparent even to a learner meeting the word for the first time.

examples.hanzi: 你明天几点考试？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ míngtiān jǐ diǎn kǎoshì?
examples.english: What time is your exam tomorrow?

examples.hanzi: 我昨晚复习到很晚，今天要考试。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuówǎn fùxí dào hěn wǎn, jīntiān yào kǎoshì.
examples.english: I studied late last night because I have an exam today.

components.note: 土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.
子 (child) — children and offspring: 孩 child, 学 study, 孙 grandchild; 存 means to keep or survive.
才 (cái) is only a loose sound hint for cún.

example.hanzi: 在沙漠里生存非常不容易。
example.pinyin: Zài shāmò lǐ shēngcún fēicháng bù róngyì.
example.english: Surviving in the desert is not easy at all.
example.fact: 生存 pairs two verbs that each independently mean roughly "to live" — 生 ("to be born, to live") and 存 ("to exist, to remain") — the same reinforcing, double-up strategy behind words like 喜欢 and 应该. 生存 leans toward survival under threat or hardship, while the far more common 生活 is the neutral word for ordinary, everyday "life."

examples.hanzi: 动物需要食物和水才能生存。
examples.pinyin: Dòngwù xūyào shíwù hé shuǐ cái néng shēngcún.
examples.english: Animals need food and water to survive.

examples.hanzi: 这家小公司在市场上很难生存。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā xiǎo gōngsī zài shìchǎng shang hěn nán shēngcún.
examples.english: It is hard for this small company to survive in the market.

components.note: 犭 (beast, form of 犬 dog) — animals: 狗 dog, 猫 cat, 狼 wolf; 犯 is to attack or violate, hence offend.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 警察正在追捕逃跑的犯人。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá zhèngzài zhuībǔ táopǎo de fànrén.
example.english: The police are chasing down the escaped convict.
example.fact: 犯 by itself is a verb meaning "to violate, to commit (an offense)," as in 犯法 ("to break the law") or 犯错 ("to make a mistake") — 犯人 simply adds 人 ("person") to name whoever did the violating, the same light noun-forming pattern behind 客人 ("guest") and 主人 ("host").

examples.hanzi: 犯人被关进了监狱。
examples.pinyin: Fànrén bèi guān jìn le jiānyù.
examples.english: The prisoner was locked up in jail.

examples.hanzi: 那个犯人终于承认了自己的错误。
examples.pinyin: Nàge fànrén zhōngyú chéngrèn le zìjǐ de cuòwù.
examples.english: The criminal finally admitted his mistake.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — calling out; 夕 (evening) beside it: in the dark you cannot be seen, so you call your name.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 这家餐厅接待过不少名人。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng jiēdài guò bùshǎo míngrén.
example.english: This restaurant has hosted quite a few celebrities.
example.fact: 名 literally means "name" but extends naturally to "fame, reputation" (as in 有名, "famous") — 名人 reads almost literally as "a name-person," someone whose name circulates widely, a similar image to how English "celebrity" traces back to Latin celeber, "thronged, famous."

examples.hanzi: 他是个名人，走到哪里都有人认识他。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì ge míngrén, zǒu dào nǎlǐ dōu yǒu rén rènshi tā.
examples.english: He is a celebrity, and people recognize him wherever he goes.

examples.hanzi: 很多名人都来参加这次慈善活动。
examples.pinyin: Hěn duō míngrén dōu lái cānjiā zhè cì císhàn huódòng.
examples.english: Many celebrities came to this charity event.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 汤, 酒; 海 is the sea.
每 (měi) — near sound — 海 is hǎi; 每 also sounds out 梅 méi and 悔 huǐ.
车 (chariot) — war chariots drawn up in a circle (the top part shows the enclosure): an army camp, hence military.

example.hanzi: 他哥哥在海军服役。
example.pinyin: Tā gēge zài hǎijūn fúyì.
example.english: His older brother serves in the navy.
example.fact: 军 alone means "army, military," and Mandarin names each service branch by pairing it with its domain: 海军 ("sea army" = navy), 陆军 ("land army" = army), 空军 ("air army" = air force) — a transparent, symmetrical naming system with no separate root words the way English has "navy," "army," and "air force."

examples.hanzi: 海军的军舰停在港口里。
examples.pinyin: Hǎijūn de jūnjiàn tíng zài gǎngkǒu lǐ.
examples.english: The navy's warships are docked in the harbor.

examples.hanzi: 他从小就想加入海军。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù xiǎng jiārù hǎijūn.
examples.english: He has wanted to join the navy since he was little.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo slips, once used for writing and lists, as in 等 wait, 笔 pen, 笑 laugh.
弟 (dì) gives the exact sound; 弟 also sounds out 梯 tī and 剃 tì.
二 (two) — the top and bottom bars. Dictionary story: five elements between heaven and earth, with a cross in the middle; memory aid, not firmly attested.

example.hanzi: 这是我今年读的第五本书。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ jīnnián dú de dìwǔ běn shū.
example.english: This is the fifth book I've read this year.
example.fact: 第 is a dedicated ordinal prefix with essentially no independent meaning outside this role — attach it to any cardinal number (一, 二, 三...) and it converts "one, two, three" into "first, second, third," functioning something like an English "-th" suffix, just placed in front of the number instead of after it.

examples.hanzi: 今天是我第五次来这里。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān shì wǒ dìwǔ cì lái zhèlǐ.
examples.english: Today is my fifth time coming here.

examples.hanzi: 我住在这栋楼的第五层。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhù zài zhè dòng lóu de dìwǔ céng.
examples.english: I live on the fifth floor of this building.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 假 is to borrow or fake, a person lending a false front.
叚 (jiǎ) sounds like 假; also in 暇 xiá and 霞 xiá.
女 (woman) — women and family terms, as in 妈 mom, 好 good, 姐 sister; 女 (nǚ) also loosely echoes the rú sound.
口 (mouth) — speech; 如 originally meant "to follow, accord with", later "as, like"; also in 汝 rǔ and 茹 rú.

example.hanzi: 假如我有很多钱,我会去世界各地旅行。
example.pinyin: Jiǎrú wǒ yǒu hěnduō qián, wǒ huì qù shìjiè gèdì lǚxíng.
example.english: If I had a lot of money, I would travel all over the world.
example.fact: 假如 sits at the more literary end of Chinese's "if" words — 如果 is the everyday default, while 假如 and its cousin 假使 feel a shade more formal or hypothetical, often signaling a scenario the speaker knows is unlikely or purely imagined, much like English "were I to..." versus plain "if I...".

examples.hanzi: 假如明天下雨，我们就不去公园了。
examples.pinyin: Jiǎrú míngtiān xià yǔ, wǒmen jiù bú qù gōngyuán le.
examples.english: If it rains tomorrow, we won't go to the park.

examples.hanzi: 假如你是我，你会怎么做？
examples.pinyin: Jiǎrú nǐ shì wǒ, nǐ huì zěnme zuò?
examples.english: If you were me, what would you do?

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and ties, as in 红, 给, 经; 结 is a knot.
吉 (jí) is a close sound clue for jié; 吉 also sounds out 洁 jié.
尺 (ruler) — the main part, as in 尺寸 size. Dictionary story: a place where measures are discussed (口), like a bureau; 局 also means 'game' as in 结局.
口 (mouth/box) — placed inside 尺. It represents talk or a space; Memory aid: a ruler fitted to a mouth means rules are discussed in an 'office'.

example.hanzi: 这部电影的结局让人很意外。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng de jiéjú ràng rén hěn yìwài.
example.english: This movie's ending is quite surprising.
example.fact: 局 by itself covers a surprisingly wide range of senses — "bureau, office" (邮局, "post office"), "situation" (局面), and "a round of a game" (一局棋, "a game of chess") — 结局 draws on that last, game-like sense: literally "how the round tied off," i.e. how the story's game played out.

examples.hanzi: 这个故事的结局很圆满。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gùshi de jiéjú hěn yuánmǎn.
examples.english: This story has a happy ending.

examples.hanzi: 没有人猜到比赛的结局。
examples.pinyin: Méiyǒu rén cāi dào bǐsài de jiéjú.
examples.english: Nobody guessed how the game would end.

components.note: 纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 线, 组; 纹 is the pattern of threads.
文 (wén) sounds exactly like 纹; also in 蚊 wén.

example.hanzi: 他的手臂上有一个纹身。
example.pinyin: Tā de shǒubì shàng yǒu yí gè wénshēn.
example.english: He has a tattoo on his arm.
example.fact: 纹 means the lines or patterns on a surface: 皱纹 (wrinkles), 指纹 (fingerprint), 花纹 (decorative pattern), 纹身 (tattoo). It rarely stands alone.

examples.hanzi: 这块布上有漂亮的花纹。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuài bù shang yǒu piàoliang de huāwén.
examples.english: This cloth has a beautiful pattern.

examples.hanzi: 他的脸上有很多皱纹。
examples.pinyin: Tā de liǎn shang yǒu hěn duō zhòuwén.
examples.english: His face has a lot of wrinkles.

components.note: 化 (change) — one person 亻 beside an upside-down person 匕 — a change of state; 化 is to change, as in 文化 and 变化.

example.hanzi: 冰化成水了。
example.pinyin: Bīng huà chéng shuǐ le.
example.english: The ice melted into water.
example.fact: 化 works like the English suffix '-ize' or '-ification': 现代化 (modernization), 全球化 (globalization), 文化 (culture). Alone it means to change or melt, and it is also in 化学 (chemistry) and 化妆 (to put on makeup).

examples.hanzi: 天气暖和了,雪都化了。
examples.pinyin: Tiānqì nuǎnhuo le, xuě dōu huà le.
examples.english: The weather got warm and the snow has all melted.

examples.hanzi: 城市的变化真大。
examples.pinyin: Chéngshì de biànhuà zhēn dà.
examples.english: The city has changed so much.

components.note: 非 (not) — two wings spread in opposite directions, so "opposed, not". Gives sound to 啡 fēi, 排 pái and 悲 bēi.
氵 (water) — water, as in 河, 海, 清: in the old form 灋, water stood for fairness, so law and method.

example.hanzi: 非法停车会被罚款。
example.pinyin: Fēifǎ tíngchē huì bèi fákuǎn.
example.english: Illegal parking will be fined.
example.fact: 非 works here as a formal negative prefix meaning "non-, not-," attaching directly to a noun the way English "il-/non-" does — 非法 ("non-law" = illegal) sits alongside similar formal compounds like 非正式 ("informal") and 非常 ("extraordinary," literally "not ordinary").

examples.hanzi: 在这里非法捕鱼是不允许的。
examples.pinyin: Zài zhèlǐ fēifǎ bǔ yú shì bù yǔnxǔ de.
examples.english: Illegal fishing is not allowed here.

examples.hanzi: 他因为非法入境被拘留了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi fēifǎ rùjìng bèi jūliú le.
examples.english: He was detained for entering the country illegally.

components.note: 合 (join) — a lid fitting over an opening 口: things that fit together. 合 also appears in 答 dá, 给 gěi and 拾 shí.
口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: voices in unison. 同 also gives sound to 铜 tóng, 桶 tǒng, 洞 dòng.

example.hanzi: 双方已经签了合同。
example.pinyin: Shuāngfāng yǐjīng qiān le hétong.
example.english: Both parties have already signed the contract.
example.fact: 合 alone means "to close, to fit together, to agree" and 同 alone means "same, together" — 合同 reads almost literally as "coming together in agreement," a fittingly on-the-nose etymology for the legal document that records exactly that.

examples.hanzi: 这份合同有三页。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn hétong yǒu sān yè.
examples.english: This contract has three pages.

examples.hanzi: 签合同之前，请先仔细看一遍。
examples.pinyin: Qiān hétong zhīqián, qǐng xiān zǐxì kàn yí biàn.
examples.english: Please read it carefully before signing the contract.

components.note: 立 (stand) — traditional 競 shows two people standing side by side in competition; 竞 keeps 立 and one 兄.
争 (contend) — simplified from 爭, two hands pulling at the same object. See 战争 war and 竞争 compete.

example.hanzi: 这两家公司之间的竞争非常激烈。
example.pinyin: Zhè liǎng jiā gōngsī zhījiān de jìngzhēng fēicháng jīliè.
example.english: The competition between these two companies is very intense.
example.fact: Both halves of 竞争 independently picture a contest: 竞's older form showed two rivals standing side by side (立 over 兄), while 争's form shows two hands (爪/彐) grabbing for the same object (亅) — 竞争 doubles up two already-vivid rivalry images into a single word.

examples.hanzi: 市场上的竞争越来越大。
examples.pinyin: Shìchǎng shang de jìngzhēng yuè lái yuè dà.
examples.english: Competition in the market is getting greater and greater.

examples.hanzi: 他们为了第一名而竞争。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen wèile dì yī míng ér jìngzhēng.
examples.english: They are competing for first place.

meanings: youngster (often affectionate, of a child or animal)

components.note: 小 (small) — three small dots, tiny grains. As a radical it appears in 少 few, 尖 sharp.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们: 伙 is a companion.
火 (huǒ, fire) gives the exact sound; 火 also means fire.

example.hanzi: 这个小家伙才三岁,已经会自己穿鞋了。
example.pinyin: Zhège xiǎojiāhuo cái sān suì, yǐjīng huì zìjǐ chuān xié le.
example.english: This little guy is only three, and he can already put his own shoes on.
example.fact: 家伙 on its own is a casual, slightly rough word for "guy, fellow" (or even "tool, weapon," depending on context) — prefixing 小 ("little") softens it into an affectionate label, most often used for a child, a pet, or anyone small enough to be called "little" without any offense meant.

examples.hanzi: 这个小家伙真可爱！
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiǎojiāhuo zhēn kě'ài!
examples.english: This little one is so cute!

examples.hanzi: 你这个小家伙，又偷吃糖了吧？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhège xiǎojiāhuo, yòu tōu chī táng le ba?
examples.english: You little rascal, you've been sneaking candy again, haven't you?

components.note: 刀 (knife) — cutting; also in 分 divide, 切 cut.
前 (qián) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 煎 jiān.

example.hanzi: 我要去剪头发。
example.pinyin: Wǒ yào qù jiǎn tóufa.
example.english: I'm going to get a haircut.
example.fact: 剪 is cutting with scissors, in contrast with 切 (qiē, to cut with a knife). 剪刀 means scissors, 剪纸 is the folk art of paper-cutting, and 剪辑 is editing video.

examples.hanzi: 请帮我剪一下指甲。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ jiǎn yíxià zhǐjia.
examples.english: Please help me trim my nails.

examples.hanzi: 你有剪刀吗?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu jiǎndāo ma?
examples.english: Do you have a pair of scissors?

components.note: 氵 (water) — liquids and flowing; 没 first meant sink or submerge (淹没), which led to "gone" and then "not have".
殳 (shū) is only a loose sound hint for 没 (méi/mò); it also sits in 设 shè and 投 tóu.
彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.
儿 (child, legs) — shows a person's legs; in 兒 the top was a child's soft skull. As an ending (这儿) it adds the er sound; 儿 also in 先, 兄, 光.

example.hanzi: “对不起,我迟到了。”“没事儿,我们才刚到。”
example.pinyin: “Duìbuqǐ, wǒ chídào le.” “Méishìr, wǒmen cái gāng dào.”
example.english: "Sorry, I'm late." "It's fine, we just got here too."
example.fact: The retroflex -儿 ending on 没事儿 is a hallmark of colloquial, Beijing-flavored Mandarin — the same phrase written without it, 没事, is understood everywhere, but 没事儿 specifically signals a relaxed, informal register, the spoken cousin of the more neutral, all-purpose 没关系 ("it doesn't matter").

examples.hanzi: 别担心，没事儿，我自己能行。
examples.pinyin: Bié dānxīn, méi shìr, wǒ zìjǐ néng xíng.
examples.english: Don't worry, it's nothing, I can manage on my own.

examples.hanzi: 你今天没事儿吧？一起去逛街怎么样？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ jīntiān méi shìr ba? Yìqǐ qù guàng jiē zěnmeyàng?
examples.english: Are you free today? How about going shopping together?

components.note: 争 (contend) — simplified from 爭, two hands pulling at the same object. See 战争 war and 竞争 compete.
耳 (ear) — a hand 又 taking an ear 耳: in ancient battle a trophy of capture. Seen in 取得 and in 娶 qǔ, 趣 qù, 最 zuì.

example.hanzi: 我们要争取更多的时间。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen yào zhēngqǔ gèng duō de shíjiān.
example.english: We need to fight for more time.
example.fact: 争取 always takes a concrete goal as its object — something you're actively working to secure, like 争取机会 ("to seek out an opportunity") or 争取时间 ("to buy time"). Its near-synonym 竞争 (also in this batch) frames the effort as a contest against a rival, while 争取 frames it as a reach toward a prize, with no opponent required.

examples.hanzi: 他一直在争取这个难得的机会。
examples.pinyin: Tā yìzhí zài zhēngqǔ zhège nándé de jīhuì.
examples.english: He has been striving for this rare opportunity.

examples.hanzi: 我们应该争取在周五之前完成。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yīnggāi zhēngqǔ zài zhōuwǔ zhīqián wánchéng.
examples.english: We should try to finish before Friday.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — 刂 is 刀 (knife) as in 到, 别, 利; 判 is to cut in half, so to separate and decide.
半 (bàn) — near sound — 判 is pàn; 半 means half.

example.hanzi: 法官判他有罪。
example.pinyin: Fǎguān pàn tā yǒu zuì.
example.english: The judge found him guilty.
example.fact: 判 appears in the language of courts and decisions: 判断 (to judge), 判决 (verdict), 审判 (trial), 判刑 (to sentence). Its idea of dividing in half connects to deciding between two sides.

examples.hanzi: 比赛的裁判判他输了。
examples.pinyin: Bǐsài de cáipàn pàn tā shū le.
examples.english: The referee ruled that he lost.

examples.hanzi: 你能判断出这是真的吗?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng pànduàn chū zhè shì zhēn de ma?
examples.english: Can you tell whether this is real?

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: receiving something by hand.
妾 (qiè) is only a loose sound clue for jiē.
下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.
来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.

example.hanzi: 接下来,我们要讨论第二个问题。
example.pinyin: Jiēxiàlái, wǒmen yào tǎolùn dì èr gè wèntí.
example.english: Next, we're going to discuss the second question.
example.fact: 接下来 functions as a transition word opening a sentence, much like English "next" or "moving on." Its literal building blocks — 接 ("to receive, to connect") plus 下来 ("coming down, continuing on") — point to an older, more concrete sense of "taking up what comes next," which has since faded into a purely sequencing function word.

examples.hanzi: 你先吃饭，接下来我们去看电影。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiān chī fàn, jiēxiàlái wǒmen qù kàn diànyǐng.
examples.english: Eat first, and then we'll go see a movie.

examples.hanzi: 接下来的几天都是晴天。
examples.pinyin: Jiēxiàlái de jǐ tiān dōu shì qíngtiān.
examples.english: The next few days will all be sunny.

components.note: 人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 人人都喜欢被称赞。
example.pinyin: Rénrén dōu xǐhuan bèi chēngzàn.
example.english: Everyone likes being praised.
example.fact: Reduplicating 人 into 人人 is one of Mandarin's simplest ways to build a universal quantifier ("every single person") with no extra grammar needed — the same doubling pattern shows up in 天天 ("every day," from 天, "day") and 家家 ("every household," from 家, "home").

examples.hanzi: 人人都应该遵守交通规则。
examples.pinyin: Rénrén dōu yīnggāi zūnshǒu jiāotōng guīzé.
examples.english: Everyone should follow the traffic rules.

examples.hanzi: 这里的饭菜人人爱吃。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de fàncài rénrén ài chī.
examples.english: Everybody loves the food here.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — the body-part radical, as in 脸, 腿, 脑; 胸 is the chest.
匈 (xiōng) gives the sound exactly: 胸 xiōng.

example.hanzi: 我的胸口有点疼。
example.pinyin: Wǒ de xiōngkǒu yǒudiǎn téng.
example.english: My chest hurts a little.
example.fact: 胸 can be physical, 胸口 (chest), or figurative, as in 胸怀 (breadth of mind). The idiom 胸有成竹, 'to have a complete bamboo in one's chest', means to be confident and well prepared.

examples.hanzi: 他挺起胸膛,大步往前走。
examples.pinyin: Tā tǐng qǐ xiōngtáng, dàbù wǎng qián zǒu.
examples.english: He puffed out his chest and strode forward.

examples.hanzi: 他胸前戴着一朵漂亮的小红花。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiōngqián dài zhe yì duǒ piàoliang de xiǎo hónghuā.
examples.english: He wore a pretty little red flower on his chest.

components.note: 车 (cart) — simplified from 車, a wheeled cart seen from above. As a radical it marks vehicles: 转 turn, 轮 wheel, 较.
礻 (spirit, omen) — 礻 is the ritual radical (示), as in 神, 礼, 福; misfortune was seen as a spirit's doing.
呙 (guō) — loose hint — 祸 is huò; 呙 also sounds out 过 guò and 锅 guō.

example.hanzi: 昨天路口发生了一起车祸。
example.pinyin: Zuótiān lùkǒu fāshēng le yì qǐ chēhuò.
example.english: A car accident happened at the intersection yesterday.
example.fact: 祸 by itself means "disaster, misfortune," and shows up across a small family of calamity words — 灾祸 ("calamity," pairing it with 灾, "disaster"), 祸害 ("bane, scourge"), and the idiom 大祸临头 ("great disaster looming"). 车祸 is simply that general "disaster" root pinned to one specific cause: the automobile.

examples.hanzi: 这场车祸让他住了一个月的院。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng chēhuò ràng tā zhù le yí ge yuè de yuàn.
examples.english: The car accident kept him in the hospital for a month.

examples.hanzi: 开车要小心，免得发生车祸。
examples.pinyin: Kāi chē yào xiǎoxīn, miǎnde fāshēng chēhuò.
examples.english: Drive carefully so you don't get into a crash.

components.note: 當 (traditional) — 田 field under 尚 (shàng), 尚 being a loose sound hint for dāng. 当 keeps only a squashed top and a few strokes of it.
尚 (shàng) — the top part of 當; only a loose sound clue today. 当 is dāng (to act as, should) or dàng (appropriate).
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 场 field, 城 city, 坐 sit.
也 (yě) is a loose sound clue for dì; 也 also sounds out 他 tā and 池 chí.

example.hanzi: 我们尝了很多当地小吃。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen cháng le hěnduō dāngdì xiǎochī.
example.english: We tried a lot of local snacks.
example.fact: 当 here means "the very one in question, this very" (as in 当时, "at that very time," or 当天, "that very day") rather than its other common sense, "to serve as" (当老师, "to work as a teacher"). 当地 leans on this less obvious reading to mean "this very place" — i.e., "local."

examples.hanzi: 当地人告诉我们哪家店最好吃。
examples.pinyin: Dāngdì rén gàosu wǒmen nǎ jiā diàn zuì hào chī.
examples.english: The locals told us which shop has the best food.

examples.hanzi: 你知道当地的天气怎么样吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhīdào dāngdì de tiānqì zěnmeyàng ma?
examples.english: Do you know what the local weather is like?

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person and his word: 言 (speech) beside it gives a person who keeps his word, hence "trust, believe".
言 (speech) — written 讠 on the left of other characters, as in 说, 请, 谢.
用 (use) — early picture is debated: a pail, a fenced enclosure or a hung bell. Memory aid: a door-frame 冂 with a cross-bar — a tool 'put to use' (使用, 不用).
上 (above) — 上 over 下 squeezed together: something stuck in the middle, the sense of qiǎ (to wedge); kǎ is the borrowed sound for "card" and "car", as in 信用卡 and 卡车.

example.hanzi: 我用信用卡付了账。
example.pinyin: Wǒ yòng xìnyòngkǎ fù le zhàng.
example.english: I paid the bill with my credit card.
example.fact: 信用 on its own means "credit, trustworthiness" (信, "trust," plus 用, "to use" — trust that can be drawn on), while 卡 is a phonetic loan character borrowed purely for its sound (kǎ, echoing English "card"). 信用卡 is a clean split between a native Chinese compound and an imported, sound-based one.

examples.hanzi: 这家店可以用信用卡吗？
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn kěyǐ yòng xìnyòngkǎ ma?
examples.english: Can I use a credit card at this shop?

examples.hanzi: 我的信用卡丢了，得马上挂失。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de xìnyòngkǎ diū le, děi mǎshàng guàshī.
examples.english: I lost my credit card and need to report it right away.

components.note: 日 (sun) — time and day, as in 时, 晚, 明: the sun at the top of a sprout, early morning. 早 also gives 草 cǎo and 澡 zǎo.
日 (sun) — 日 is the sun and time of day, as in 明, 晚, 早; 晨 is early morning.
辰 (chén) — same sound — 晨 is chén, like 辰.

example.hanzi: 他每天早晨都去跑步。
example.pinyin: Tā měitiān zǎochén dōu qù pǎobù.
example.english: He goes running every morning.
example.fact: 早 and 晨 both independently mean roughly "morning, early," and both are built around 日 (the sun) — 早 shows the sun 日 with the first rays 十 breaking near the horizon, while 晨 pairs 日 with the phonetic 辰. 早晨 reinforces two sun-based dawn images into one everyday word for "morning."

examples.hanzi: 早晨的空气特别新鲜。
examples.pinyin: Zǎochen de kōngqì tèbié xīnxiān.
examples.english: The air is especially fresh in the early morning.

examples.hanzi: 明天早晨六点，我们在门口见面。
examples.pinyin: Míngtiān zǎochen liù diǎn, wǒmen zài ménkǒu jiànmiàn.
examples.english: Tomorrow morning at six, let's meet at the door.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海; 滚 is to roll like boiling water.
衮 (gǔn) — same sound — 滚 is gǔn, like 衮.
廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).

example.hanzi: 水已经滚开了,可以下面条了。
example.pinyin: Shuǐ yǐjīng gǔnkāi le, kěyǐ xià miàntiáo le.
example.english: The water is already boiling, so we can put the noodles in.
example.fact: 滚开 leads a double life: said of water or another liquid, it's a neutral, everyday way to say "boiling," but shouted at a person it becomes a genuinely rude command to leave, on the same level as English "get lost" or worse — tone of voice and context do all the disambiguating work.

examples.hanzi: 把滚开的水倒进杯子里。
examples.pinyin: Bǎ gǔnkāi de shuǐ dào jìn bēizi lǐ.
examples.english: Pour the boiling water into the cup.

examples.hanzi: 小心，锅里的汤滚开了。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn, guō lǐ de tāng gǔnkāi le.
examples.english: Careful, the soup in the pot is boiling.

components.note: 彳 (step) — the left part and radical, as in 往 and 行. It suggests going step by step; in 微 'tiny', as in 微笑 smile. Rest of the shape is unclear.
攵 (tap) — the bottom-right part, as in 收. Memory aid: tapping very lightly with tiny steps, so everything is 'slight'.
夭 (yāo) is a loose sound clue for xiào; 夭 also in 妖 yāo. The bamboo top ⺮ here is a historical shape, not a meaning clue.

example.hanzi: 她对我微笑了一下。
example.pinyin: Tā duì wǒ wēixiào le yíxià.
example.english: She smiled at me briefly.
example.fact: 微 contributes the sense "slight, faint" (as in 微小, "tiny," or 微风, "a gentle breeze") to 笑 ("to laugh, to smile"). 微笑 is specifically the quiet, closed-mouth smile, set apart from a bigger, sound-making 大笑 ("to laugh out loud") by that one modifying character.

examples.hanzi: 她总是带着微笑跟客人打招呼。
examples.pinyin: Tā zǒngshì dài zhe wēixiào gēn kèrén dǎ zhāohu.
examples.english: She always greets guests with a smile.

examples.hanzi: 看到孩子们，老师微笑着点了点头。
examples.pinyin: Kàndào háizimen, lǎoshī wēixiào zhe diǎn le diǎn tóu.
examples.english: Seeing the children, the teacher nodded with a smile.

meanings: I, me (used to refer to oneself)

components.note: 人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.

example.hanzi: 别管人家怎么想,做你自己觉得对的事。
example.pinyin: Bié guǎn rénjia zěnme xiǎng, zuò nǐ zìjǐ juéde duì de shì.
example.english: Don't worry about what other people think — do what you feel is right.
example.fact: 人家 hides two different words under one spelling. Read with a full tone on 家 (rén jiā), it's the literal, more formal "household, family." But in everyday speech, said with a light, neutral-toned jia (rén jia), it becomes a colloquial pronoun meaning "other people," "he/she/they," or even a coy stand-in for "I, me" — the reading pulled here is that common colloquial one, not the literal "household" sense.

examples.hanzi: 人家已经等了你半个小时了。
examples.pinyin: Rénjia yǐjīng děng le nǐ bàn ge xiǎoshí le.
examples.english: I've already been waiting for you for half an hour.

examples.hanzi: 这是人家送给我的礼物，不能随便送人。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì rénjia sòng gěi wǒ de lǐwù, bù néng suíbiàn sòng rén.
examples.english: This is a gift someone gave me, so I can't just give it away.

components.note: 电 (electric) — simplified from 電: 雨 rain over 申, a lightning bolt (申 originally pictured a flash).
木 (wood) — 木 is wood, as in 桌, 板; a ladder was a wooden structure.
弟 (dì) — near sound — 梯 is tī; 弟 also sounds out 第 dì and 递 dì.

example.hanzi: 电梯坏了,我们只能走楼梯。
example.pinyin: Diàntī huài le, wǒmen zhǐnéng zǒu lóutī.
example.english: The elevator is broken, so we have to take the stairs.
example.fact: 梯 alone already means "ladder, steps" (as in 楼梯, "stairs") — 电 ("electricity") simply modifies it to name the powered version, the same modifying pattern behind 电话 ("electric speech" = telephone) and 电脑 ("electric brain" = computer).

examples.hanzi: 这栋楼没有电梯，我每天爬六层楼。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dòng lóu méiyǒu diàntī, wǒ měi tiān pá liù céng lóu.
examples.english: This building has no elevator, so I climb six floors every day.

examples.hanzi: 我们在电梯里碰到了邻居。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài diàntī lǐ pèngdào le línjū.
examples.english: We ran into a neighbor in the elevator.
